prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the pii-chat agent (card support: identity checks, lost and stolen cards, replacements) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: sight loss and reading card numbers. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member says they have sight loss, I should not assume they can read back card numbers in the usual way; I need to slow the identity check down and offer a simpler route from the outset."},{"type":"fact","content":"When card details need to be confirmed, I should avoid asking the member to read the full number unless they have said they are comfortable doing so; if not, I should use an alternative verification step instead."},{"type":"preference","content":"When sight loss affects reading, I should prefer short, one-step questions and give the member time to answer without rushing or repeating the full sequence too quickly."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member cannot read the card number on the front, I should check whether they have another way to find it, such as a statement or digital banking, before moving on to replacement options."},{"type":"fact","content":"When identity checks are incomplete because the card number cannot be read, I can still help by verifying the member through other account details that do not depend on sight of the card."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a card is lost or stolen and the member has sight loss, I should keep the explanation of next steps clear and ordered, because a calm, structured call reduces confusion."},{"type":"observation","content":"When reading a card number is difficult, I should say numbers back in small groups rather than all at once, and confirm each group before continuing."},{"type":"fact","content":"When arranging a replacement card, I should note any accessibility need so the next interaction starts with the right support and does not repeat the same difficulty."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member asks for help with card details, I should offer practical options such as texting, secure message, or another accessible route, rather than assuming voice-only support will be easiest."},{"type":"observation","content":"When sight loss is mentioned early, it is better to treat it as relevant context for the whole card-support journey, not just a note for identity checks, because it can affect replacements, PIN reminders, and follow-up contact."}]}
